title: Full pool — the UI wallet wins, and takes the entire prize pool
hypothesis: A pool that reaches 64 entrants seals on the 64th register (SealReason::Capacity), not at its deadline. The crank then reveals the pool secret, decrypts and verifies every sealed allocation, scores all-vs-all, commits one results root and one payout row, and pays it. PAID_RANKS is 1, so the single rank-1 seat takes the WHOLE 4 SOL pot and nobody ranked second or lower is paid a lamport. The field is engineered so that outcome is arithmetic rather than luck: UI-A plays a wall, UI-B plays a pole, and the other 62 seats are capped at 25 on every stat.

unconditionalDerivation._: Why UI-A must win and UI-B must come last, from the shapes alone — no seed, no exact numbers.
unconditionalDerivation.scoringRule: A stat goes to the larger number. A battle goes to whoever wins at least 3 of 5 stats, otherwise it is a draw. Score is 2 half-points a win, 1 a draw, across all 7 battles against each of the other 63 entrants.
unconditionalDerivation.wallBeatsField: A wall holds three stats at 26 or above; no field seat exceeds 25. So the wall wins those three stats against every field seat in every battle, which is >= 3 of 5, so it wins every one of 434 battles against the field: 868 half-points.
unconditionalDerivation.wallNeverLosesToPole: Against a pole the wall wins at least 2 stats (the pole holds one stat, and its spike either lands on a wall stat, leaving the wall 2 and the pole 1 with two 0-0 ties and nobody at 3 — a draw — or on a wall zero, leaving the wall 3 and a win). So the wall takes at least 1 half-point per battle there: its floor is 875 = 868 + 7.
unconditionalDerivation.fieldCeiling: Every field seat loses all 7 battles to the wall, so the best it can reach is 854 against the other 61 field seats plus 14 against the pole = 868, which is below the wall's floor of 875. The wall is rank 1 whatever the field does.
unconditionalDerivation.poleFloor: Every field seat beats the pole in every battle (5 nonzero stats against 1 wins 4 stats), so the pole scores 0 against all 62 of them and at most 7 against the wall — at most 7. The worst any field seat can do is 14 from the pole alone, which is more. The pole is strictly last whatever the field does.

expectations.sealReason: Capacity — the 64th register seals the pool immediately; seal_at_deadline is never called
expectations.vaultAfterNote: the rent cushion, never recovered. The pot leaves the vault in full and the cushion stays.
expectations.treasuryNote: 1995448320 + 64 x 100000000 entries. Pool 15 was pre-funded before this test began, so the 4.00065 SOL that left the treasury at open is already out and is not counted again.
expectations.winnerNetNote: 4000000000 prize minus the 104436000 the entry and its rent cost.
expectations.conditionalNote: The root and the leaf order assume entries land in the planned seat order AND that UI-A and UI-B enter the exact sets named below. A rank never depends on either: ranks fall out of the allocations alone. If the seat order or a UI allocation differs, the unconditional expectations still stand and these two are recorded as drift, not as a failure.
detectionNotes: Detection computes and PERSISTS a report for the pool but flags nobody: the daemon hook returns an empty list under the manual-only policy ruling D-E9. No flag, no escrow, no delay to the payout.
population_score is predicted to fire on UI-A. It is many sigma from the field by design — that is the point of the test, and finding it there is a detection PASS, not a fault.
allocation_entropy is predicted to raise its round-number note on UI-B: a pole is all zeroes and a hundred, so 100% of its stat values are multiples of ten.
allocation_entropy must NOT fire "strong" on anyone: every seat carries at least 3 distinct shapes across its 7 battles (UI-A has 7, UI-B has 5, the field has 7 each).
duplicate_sets must not fire: all 64 seven-battle sets are distinct, asserted by validate-plan.ts before the freeze.
A detectionReviewRecommended alert is expected. It is an alert, not a block.

Sanctions screening runs on the winner before payment (Stage F). UI-A is a fresh devnet embedded wallet and no match is expected. A hold would escrow the prize instead of paying it — that is the one predicted-benign step that could delay settlement, and it would be recorded rather than worked around.

seats.recipe: each battle, drag two stats to 0 — pairs in order: Strength+Speed, Speed+Heart, Heart+Wit, Wit+Durability, Durability+Strength, Strength+Heart, Speed+Wit
each battle, drag one stat to 100 — in order: Strength, Speed, Heart, Wit, Durability, Heart, Strength

seatNote: `seat` is null until the pool runs: the index is assigned by register order and harvest.ts records what actually happened. `plannedSeat` is the index this plan assumes, and only the root and leaf order depend on it.
contingency: If fewer than 64 seats land before the 01:52:26Z deadline, the pool seals at whatever it holds provided that is at least 40, and still plays and pays. The engineered ranks are unaffected — a smaller field changes the scores, not who wins. Reconcile against the seats that actually entered.
If fewer than 40 land, the pool refunds and T4 is NOT a scored test. It would be rerun on the next pool rather than recorded as a failure of the product.
If the founder enters a legal set that is not the one named here, the unconditional expectations hold and the two UI seats reconcile as INPUT_DRIFT.

If the run clock expires on an unlocked battle it is entered as the EVEN SPLIT [20,20,20,20,20], which is neither a wall nor a pole. That is the single most likely way this test breaks, and it is why the founder instruction is two drags a battle and lock in each one.
passCriteria: Exactly one seat is paid, it is UI-A, and the amount is the whole 4000000000 lamport pot.
The results root recomputed from the published bundle equals the on-chain results_root.
The vault ends at 650240 lamports and the treasury at 8395448320.
No seat is flagged and no sanctions hold is placed.
